topics.label: Citizenship Certificate
topics.seoTitle: Canadian Citizenship Certificate 2026: Apply or Replace | CMG
topics.metaDescription: How to obtain proof of Canadian citizenship — new certificate applications and replacements for lost, stolen, or damaged documents.
topics.lead: A citizenship certificate is the official document proving Canadian citizenship, needed for passport applications and other government processes — this covers both first-time applications for those who acquired citizenship without one, and replacements for lost or damaged certificates.

topics.label: Citizenship Resumption
topics.metaDescription: Reclaim Canadian citizenship after it was lost or renounced — eligibility and the resumption application process explained.
topics.lead: Citizenship resumption is the process for former Canadian citizens — who lost citizenship through renunciation or an older rule that no longer applies — to reclaim their status, generally through a defined application process rather than starting over as a new applicant.

topics.label: Citizenship Renunciation
topics.metaDescription: How to formally renounce Canadian citizenship — eligibility conditions and why applicants typically pursue this process.
topics.lead: Citizenship renunciation is the formal process of voluntarily giving up Canadian citizenship, generally pursued by dual citizens who need to satisfy another country's requirements or who no longer wish to hold Canadian status.

topics.label: Citizenship Revocation Appeal
topics.metaDescription: Facing citizenship revocation for misrepresentation or fraud? Understand the process and your appeal or review options.
topics.lead: Citizenship revocation is a serious process where the government seeks to remove citizenship already granted, most commonly on grounds of fraud or material misrepresentation during the original application. Individuals facing revocation have defined rights to respond and, in many cases, seek review.

topics.label: PR Card Renewal & Citizenship (combined overview)
topics.seoTitle: PR Card Renewal & Canadian Citizenship 2026 | CMG
topics.metaDescription: PR card renewal, residency obligation rules, and Canadian citizenship application requirements — physical presence, language, and test prep.
topics.lead: Once granted permanent residence, staying in status means meeting an ongoing residency obligation and keeping a valid PR card for travel. Citizenship is the natural next step for permanent residents who meet Canada's physical presence and other eligibility requirements.

topics.label: PR Card Renewal — standalone page
topics.metaDescription: How to renew your Permanent Resident Card: residency obligation check, processing times, and how early to apply before expiry.
topics.lead: A PR card is generally valid for 5 years and must be renewed to continue using it as proof of status for travel and re-entry to Canada. Renewal also involves confirming the holder still meets the residency obligation.

topics.label: PR Card Replacement
topics.metaDescription: Lost, stolen, or damaged PR card? Replacement application process and how to travel in the meantime.
topics.lead: A lost, stolen, or damaged PR card needs to be replaced through a dedicated application, distinct from a standard renewal — since the card may still be within its validity period when replacement becomes necessary.

topics.label: PR Travel Document (PRTD)
topics.metaDescription: PRTD application process for permanent residents abroad without a valid PR card — requirements and processing at Canadian visa offices.
topics.lead: A Permanent Resident Travel Document (PRTD) allows a permanent resident outside Canada without a valid PR card to board a flight back to Canada — applied for through the Canadian visa office responsible for the applicant's location.
